Это довольно незамысловатая игрушка, где скидывая карты влево или вправо, т.е. как бы говоря да или нет, нужно держать баланс четырёх сторон - армии, народа, церкви и денег. Причём именно баланс, примерно по центру каждой шкалы, ибо как только одна из них достигнет верхней или нижней точки, вы умрёте, так или иначе. И да, это будет не конец игры, ибо фактически вы играете за династию и у игры есть свой "таймлайн", но вот ваши короли это буквально расходники, что просто спавнятся из воздуха. Игру можно "пройти" тупо скипая все карты чисто рандомно и да, короли будут жить секунды при этом, но "сюжет" будет длиться "неизбежно". Как-то так.

Почему сюжет в кавычках? Да его буквально нет, вот и всё. Вы просто играете в рамках игры до 1998го года, после чего она так или иначе кончается и стартует заново. У игры скорее есть местные микро-истории, оборотни там, пророк, крестовый поход. Но они также очень маленькие и поверхностные. Но это как бы и не удивительно, сложно закрутить экшония в односложных фразах и ответах да/нет на них.

Интересно ли это было? Нуууу, нормально. Играть можно, как минимум. Правда не на ПК, ибо это просто странно за ним ощущается, как какая-то потеря времени. Вот как рогаликоподобная залипушка для смартфона в дорогу - вот тут вообще отлично, было бы.
Да и скучновато быстро становится, персы одинаковые, событий не сказать что прям много, очень быстро всё выходит на бесконечные самоповторы даже в рамках одной династии. Тем более игра не сказать, что про стратегическое мышление какое-то, это буквально рандомная тыкалка без особых последствий. Типа 10 лет ты проживёшь, 50, да хоть 100, но рано или поздно выпадет карта, которая сломает жизнь очередному безликому королю, как ты не вертись, просто вот на рандоме. Но в любом случае, один-два раза чего бы и не сыграть?

Хотя, всё же есть у игры и более серьёзный минус - ачивки, по традиции гениев на разрабах. Всякие смерти, концовки и прочая дичь. Но главное - увидеть в районе так 850ти карт. Это много, скажу я вам. И повлиять на это особо нельзя, чисто рандом, ради которого игру возможно придётся "проходить" несколько десятков раз, ловя новые карты по одной-две штуки на всю "историю". Тупо, уныло, долго.

В общем-то, в итоге, сама игра меня более-менее устроила. Но вот иные игры "серии" я что-то не хочу брать больше (хотя изначально планы такие были). И не только из-за "боязни" ачивок, просто не видится особого смысла в том, чтобы играть в них на ПК.

I thought being a King meant power, wealth, and respect. Turns out, it’s just me sitting on a throne, swiping left and right on people’s problems like I’m looking for a date on a Friday night.

The balance in this game is impossible. If I give the people a loaf of bread, the Church gets offended and burns me at the stake. If I tell the Army to relax, the neighboring kingdom invades and turns my head into a decorative vase. If I try to be a "nice guy," I get trampled by a mob. If I’m too rich, I choke on a golden pigeon during a feast.

I’ve died in 45 different ways in under 20 minutes. My legacy isn't "The Great" or "The Conqueror"—it’s "The Guy Who Got Eaten by His Own Dog Because He Was Too Polite."

The gameplay works like Tinder, with relatively simple "yes" or "no" decisions by swiping left or right. The idea is incredibly ingenious

The problem is that to see the true ending (the thing that achieves all the concept to make sense), you have to figure out exactly what to do and just then, try to do it (because yes, there's a fair chance of failure, including a couple of things dependent on RNG), which means about three to Five full playthroughs (with luck). This, for me, is a pretty big design flaw because it feels awful to have to play another hour and a half just to kill the run that didn't work and start from scratch. It's what keeps me from buying more games of this type. Otherwise, it's pretty cool.

Reigns es, básicamente, Tinder medieval… pero cada match puede terminar en tu ejecución.

La premisa es gloriosamente absurda: sos un rey (o reina) y gobernás un reino deslizando cartas a izquierda o derecha. ¿Aceptás la propuesta de la Iglesia? Deslizá. ¿Le hacés caso al general sospechosamente entusiasta por ir a la guerra? Deslizá. ¿Adoptás un gato poseído que habla en acertijos? Bueno… también deslizá.

El problema —y la magia— es que todo tiene consecuencias ridículamente exageradas. Si apoyás demasiado a la Iglesia, te convertís en un fanático. Si ignorás al pueblo, te derrocan. Si acumulás demasiado dinero, alguien decide que eso es sospechoso. Y si intentás mantener el equilibrio perfecto… igual algo va a salir mal, porque el juego parece diseñado por un bufón con complejo de guionista trágico.

Cada partida dura pocos minutos y casi siempre termina con una muerte absurda: envenenado, traicionado, devorado, maldecido, aplastado por tu propio ego… y volvés a empezar como si nada. Es un bucle eterno de decisiones cuestionables y finales aún más cuestionables.

Lo mejor es el tono. Reigns no se toma en serio ni por un segundo. Hay demonios, papas rarísimos, científicos adelantados a su época, conspiraciones ridículas y situaciones que escalan de “problema administrativo” a “apocalipsis total” en tres decisiones mal dadas.

En el fondo es un juego de gestión y equilibrio, sí. Pero también es una comedia negra interactiva donde aprendés que gobernar es imposible y que, honestamente, quizás el reino estaría mejor sin vos.

This one has the most basic gameplay of all the Reigns games, but I don't think that's a bad thing. Some of the other games get overly complicated and forget the appeal of the original, which is balancing all four meters by making yes or no choices. 
There's also a LOT of cards, and situations can change based on the choices you make. 
There's also multiple endings! The best ending is kind of hard to figure out, but not impossible.

It's incredible how such a simple concept of just swiping left or right to decide can produce such a fun game with so many possible outcomes. This game is all about experimenting with your choices and balancing the powers in order to keep your character(s) alive as long as possible and, hopefully, being able to eventually reach the good ending.

Reigns parte de uma ideia muito criativa e simples: tomar decisões apenas deslizando cartas para a esquerda ou direita. Funciona perfeitamente como um passatempo rápido, mas com uma camada interessante de profundidade, já que o jogador precisa equilibrar constantemente os pilares do reino e pensar nas consequências das escolhas a médio e longo prazo.

A narrativa e o humor funcionam muito bem dentro dessa proposta. Os eventos são bastante aleatórios, mas as decisões têm impacto real no andamento da partida, o que evita que tudo pareça puramente caótico. Não há um final definitivo, e o objetivo passa a ser ver o quanto você consegue sobreviver, mas em poucas horas já é possível ter contato com grande parte das situações e possibilidades.

A repetição aparece mais para quem tenta desbloquear todas as conquistas, já que isso exige várias tentativas semelhantes, mas nada chega a ser realmente cansativo. No geral, é um jogo que sabe exatamente o que quer ser: um passatempo casual, inteligente e bem executado, sem pretensão de ir além disso.

Introduction:
Reigns places players in the role of a monarch navigating the complex politics, whims, and perils of ruling a kingdom. Through a clever card-swipe mechanic, each choice carries consequences that can shift the balance of power, wealth, faith, and military might. What seems like a simple interface quickly reveals a deeply engaging system of cause and effect, making Reigns a thoughtful and addictive take on decision-making and narrative strategy.

Gameplay (4/5):
Reigns’ gameplay is deceptively simple: swipe left or right to make decisions presented on cards. But beneath that simplicity lies a rich web of outcomes and branching paths. Each choice you make affects four core pillars of your reign—church, people, army, and treasury—and maintaining balance is both strategically satisfying and narratively impactful. The pacing is brisk, and the feedback is immediate, keeping you invested in the consequences of every decision. Graphics and Sound (3.5/5):

Immersion and Atmosphere (4.5/5):

You quickly find yourself invested in the fate of your kingdom, laughing at absurd events, and grimacing at disastrous choices. The writing is sharp, witty, and unpredictable, giving each reign a unique flavor with memorable moments that range from whimsical to darkly thoughtful. Replay Value (4/5):

There’s a satisfying sense of discovery as you unlock more narrative threads and uncover hidden outcomes. While some events loop back or recur, the variety across dozens of decisions keeps multiple playthroughs feeling fresh and rewarding.

Conclusion:
Reigns is an elegant blend of simplicity and narrative complexity. Its mechanics are easy to grasp but rich in consequence, and the writing elevates what could have been a basic decision game into something much more memorable. While it doesn’t rely on cutting-edge visuals or complex systems, its charm and depth make it a standout in the genre. For players who enjoy thoughtful choice, emergent storytelling, and replayable strategy with a sense of humor, Reigns is a crown worth wearing. 👑

Things I like:
- Minimalistic art style is charming and "clean". Animations are smooth.
- Sound effects / sound design is minimal but does the job; fake voices / accents are funny.
- The dialogue / writing is quite good, for what it is. Definitely helps to carry the story forward.
- The tinder-style interface, coupled with the YES/NO binary choice system is not that bad, and can work well in "choice A choice B" situations.

Things that don't work:
- Remember that Choice A / B thing I mentioned? Well, the UI of the game forces you to use this, but some answers just "don't work" on a practical basis; some scenario cards are "funny" and have no real "right answer", and some are super specific where you need to do the right set of choices or fail miserably. Interspersed between these two extremes are the "realistic choices" where something goes up and something goes down, and that's only where the UI is most effective.
- It's ridiculous to not show me how much of a + and - modifer I'm getting on my current stats before I make a decision. It's already a guess anyways given the writing, but only seeing a "small circle" or "big circle" on one of my stats and forcing me to guess the outcome does not feel rewarding at all. I am aware that the game DOES have a secret bonus where you CAN see the consequence effects on stats, but this should be something you START with, not something you have to scramble for to make better decisions.

TLDR;
The game has a design/identity crisis between either being:
1. A strategic Choice A/B simulator where you need to think carefully about your compromises and governance strategies to stay in power; machiavellian power plays, etc, where YOU know the outcomes on your decisions.
2. A choose-your-own adventure game, where it takes funny twists and turns, and you're along for the ride with minimal decision making.

The best way to enjoy this game is to pick option 2), and then do a LITTLE bit of option 1) when the game requires you to do so. Just try to enjoy the writing / narrative and all the funny and odd bits, and ignore the replayability; the developer's strength was clearly the funny, interactive moments and not the strategic design.
